narrative:
The model estimates a 70% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key aspects of your professional profile.

Your total years of experience across all jobs stands out as the strongest factor pushing the model toward predicting you will leave. With 6-10 years of overall experience, you fall into a group where many professionals start exploring new opportunities, unlike the majority of those predicted to stay, who tend to have only 1-5 years.

Next, the model noted that you have not received any other job offers while at your current organization. This actually works in your favor and pulls the prediction slightly back toward staying, as employees who do receive external offers are far more likely to depart.

The third most influential factor is the relatively short time you have spent in your current role—1 to 5 years. This shorter tenure in your present position also increases the likelihood of leaving according to the model, as longer-serving employees in the same organization are more likely to remain.

Taken together, your broad experience combined with limited time at this specific organization appears to signal higher mobility risk, outweighing the stabilizing effect of not having competing offers. The organization should consider discussing your career goals with you directly and exploring ways to increase your sense of long-term stability here. You, in turn, may want to reflect on whether your experience level has prepared you for a new chapter.
